senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; cmp. <cite ref="B00752">preced.</cite>; v. Ges. H. Dict. s. v. as to various etymological attempts), constr. <cite ref="B00754"><he>בֵּית</he></cite>, pl. <he>בָּתִּים</he>.

units: Yoma 11ᵇ ב׳ מיוחד לדירה bayith means a building intended for a dwelling.

Ib. מי שמייחד ביתו לו (Var. v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) he who devotes his house (its contents) to himself exclusively (unaccommodating); Arakh. 16ᵃ מי שמיוחד וכ׳.—בעל הב׳ (abbrev. בע״ה) owner, landlord; host; private man, opp. to trader, artisan &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 46a:1">Ber. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>בע״ה בוצע וכ׳</he> the host breaks the bread, and the guest says the blessing.
<cite ref="Tosefta Berakhot 4:14">Tosef. ib. IV, 14</cite> <he>של בע״ה</he> home-made (bread), opp. <cite ref="C00910"><he>גלוסקין</he></cite>; Y. ib. VI, 10ᵇ bot.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:1">Sabb. I, 1</cite> <he>בע״ה</he> the donor, opp. <cite ref="P00970"><he>עני</he></cite> the recipient.
Gen. R. s. 22; a. v. fr.—בן ב׳ inmate, attendant.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:5">Ab. I, 5</cite>; a. fr.—<he>פסול הב׳</he> the degraded (slave) of the house.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:13">Gen. R. s. 70</cite>.

senses.gloss: Esp. (הַ)בַּ׳ the Temple. בפני הב׳ in days when the Temple exists, שלא בפני הב׳ when it does not exist.
units: Ḥull. V, 1; a. fr.—ב׳ שני or ב׳ אחרון the Second Temple.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:9:3">Cant. R. to VIII, 9</cite>; a. fr.—<he>הר הב׳</he> Temple Mount, v. <cite ref="E00808"><he>הַר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 1:1">Bets. I, 1</cite>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Tractate Soferim 4:1">Treat. Sof’rim IV, 1</cite> <he>של ב׳ וכ׳</he> those of the house of &c. [<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 2:2:2">Y. Shebi. II, 33ᵈ</cite> bot., a. e. <he>דבית … ר׳</he>, usu. <cite ref="D00056"><he>דבי</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="B00536"><he>בֵּי</he></cite>].
<cite ref="Berakhot 44b:10">Ber. 44ᵇ</cite> <he>אוי לו לב׳ וכ׳</he> that human body (Rashi: stomach) is to be pitied where vegetables are a constant guest (being the only food).
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:1">Yoma I, 1</cite> <he>ביתו זו וכ׳</he> ‘his house’—that means his wife.
<cite ref="Yoma 13a:6">Ib. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>והך לאו ביתו היא</he> but this one (designated for him in case of his wife’s death) cannot be called ‘his house’.
<cite ref="Shabbat 118b:7">Sabb. 118ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 9:3:3">Y. Sabb. IX, 12ᵃ</cite> top; <cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 8:4">Mikv. VIII, 4</cite> <he>שמשה את בֵּיתָהּ</he> she had intercourse.
<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 8:4">Ib.</cite> <he>כבדה את הב׳</he> she washed &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 1:2:1">Y. Sot. I, 16ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אסורה לביתה</he> is forbidden to her husband.
<cite ref="Niddah 5a">Nidd. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>מהומת לביתה</he> she hastens to perform her marital duty. Y. ib. I, beg. 48ᵈ. Cmp. <cite ref="H00214"><he>חֶדֶר</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: store-house, store-room. בֵּית העצים wood-room; ב׳ התבן straw-magazine; ב׳ הבקר stable; &c.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 11a:14">Yoma 11ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (geogr.) place, town, in compounds (for which see the respective determinants), e.g. ב׳ בוקיא Beth-Bukya &c.
(anat.) limb, organ, in compounds (v. supra 8)), e.g. ב׳ הבליעה œsophagus, &c.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 2:4">Shebi. II, 4</cite> (pl.). Y. ib. 33ᵈ.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:20">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵃ</cite>.—1
Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. IV, 11; ב׳ יד sleeve, v. אוּנְקְלַי II, &c.—
Men. 34ᵇ, a. e. cases of the T’fillin
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 38a:2">Snh. 38ᵃ</cite> <he>שני ב׳ א׳</he> two families (dynasties); a. fr.—
Tosef. Ter. II, 11 בתי אבות = אריסי ב׳ א׳ hereditary land-tenants; B. Bath. 46ᵇ
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 2:6">Taan. II, 6</cite>; a. fr.; v. <cite ref="A02149"><he>אֱנוֹשׁ</he></cite> pl.

senses.gloss: origin of a law, rule &c.; cmp. אָב II.
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4:1">Cant. R. to II, 4</cite> <he>ב׳ א׳ של הלכה</he> the origin (principle) of a legal rule.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 118:19">Midr. Till. to Ps. CIV, 29</cite> wherever the root <he>רעש</he> is used, it means cessation of government, <he>ואיזהו ב׳ א׳ שלהם וכ׳</he> and where is the origin (determining the meaning) of all of them? (Answ.
<cite ref="Jeremiah 51:29">Jer. LI, 29</cite>).

Lev. R. s. 1, beg. מב׳ א׳ שלהן וכ׳ from the chief passage (Hag. I, 13 ‘Haggai, the messenger’ &c.) we learn that prophets are called messengers (or angels).—בֵּית דִּין (abbr. ב״ד) court.—ב״ד של שבעים ואחד or ב״ד הגדול the Great Sanedrin of seventy one members.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 1:5">Snh. I, 5</cite>. Y. ib. 19ᵃ bot.; a. fr.—<he>ב״ד נוטה</he> court of an odd number of judges. <he>ב״ד שקול</he> of an even number of judges.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 3b:17">Snh. 3ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ב״ד שריא</he> a permitting court, opprobrious name of a court too lax in religious affairs. Y. Gitt. VII, 48ᵈ top; Y. Nidd. III, 50ᵈ bot.—[For all other compounds not self-evident, v. respective determinants.] [<he>בית תר</he>, v. <cite ref="B00764"><he>בִּיתֵּר</he></cite>.—
